passage: Wednesday. Sudha walked into class today wearing her yellow hairband, and my heart did a big jump. When Sir asked me to read, I forgot my own name. Then she said, "Can I borrow your ruler?" and I just nodded like a bobblehead. Ugh 😅. I wanted to say something clever. Maybe tomorrow I will say a normal good morning, like I do to everyone. I will not stare at her or follow her around at recess, because that would be weird and not fair to her. It is a funny, warm feeling, and there is nothing wrong with having it. -- Mohit

qa.q: How was Mohit feeling when Sudha asked to borrow a ruler?
qa.a: Mohit was flustered and shy, able only to nod for lack of words, and Mohit's heart had jumped when she walked in.

qa.q: What is Mohit's plan for handling this shyness respectfully?
qa.a: Mohit plans to say a normal good morning as with everyone, and not to stare at her or follow her at recess.

qa.q: How might Sudha see Mohit's nodding when she asks for the ruler?
qa.a: She probably just sees Mohit lending a ruler, without knowing Mohit's feelings, since Mohit only nodded.

grounding: A child's first crush leaves the child tongue-tied, with a plan to be friendly and give her space.

passage:
Monday. Mahima walked into the art room, and Jatin's heart jumped. He opened his mouth to say hi, and nothing came out. He stared at his paintbrush instead, face hot.
Wednesday. Jatin noticed he'd been watching the door, waiting for her. He made himself stop. He didn't want to be weird about it. It was a nice feeling, not a bad one.
Friday. In art, Mahima asked, "Can I borrow your blue?"
Jatin handed it over. "Sure. Your river painting's really good."
"Thanks!" she said, and went back to her seat.
Jatin grinned at his paper. That was enough. Just friendly.

qa.q: What did Mahima ask to borrow?
What was Jatin feeling on Monday when Mahima walked in?
qa.a: He felt shy and flustered, his heart jumping and his face hot, unable to speak.

qa.q: What did Jatin do that kept things comfortable?
qa.a: He stopped watching the door, and when Mahima spoke to him he was simply friendly and kept it light.

qa.q: How might Mahima see Jatin's compliment?
qa.a: Mahima probably sees it as a friendly, kind comment, since she thanks him and goes back to her seat.

grounding: A boy's heart jumps when a girl walks in and he cannot speak; he treats the crush as a nice feeling, avoids staring and keeps things friendly and light.

passage:
"Rehana, your Rukmini Paati remembers when my little brother Mohan had his first crush. He was eleven. A girl called Vasuki joined his class, and suddenly Mohan couldn't say a word when she was near. He went red as a tomato.
He was so embarrassed, he wanted to hide in the loft. I told him, 'This is a sweet feeling. There is no shame in it.'
Then I told him the rules: 'Be friendly, and keep things light. Don't stare, and don't follow her around.'
He listened. He started saying 'good morning' to Vasuki, just like to anyone else. By the end of the year they were good friends, and that was that."

qa.q: What was the name of the girl Mohan liked?
How did Mohan feel when Vasuki was near?
qa.a: He felt shy and embarrassed, going red as a tomato and wanting to hide in the loft.

qa.q: What choice in the story helped Mohan handle his crush well?
qa.a: Following his sister's advice to be friendly, keep things light and not stare or follow Vasuki, so he started simply saying good morning.

qa.q: How might Vasuki have seen Mohan's 'good morning'?
qa.a: Vasuki likely saw it as ordinary friendliness, which let them become good friends.

grounding: A grandmother recalls her brother's first crush, when he could not speak near a girl, and how he learned to be friendly and light without staring or following her.
